News.title: Frail mum's screams as XL bullies son-in-law left her with mauled her to death
News.content:
Frail mum's screams as XL bullies son-in-law left her with mauled her to death

Esther Martin, 68, was left to look after two XL Bullies and eight puppies despite her frail condition when she was horrifically mauled to death at the home of Ashley Warren who has been jailed

View 4 Images Esther Martin was mauled to death (Image: PA)

A frail pensioner was heard screaming as she suffered “dozens and dozens’ of injuries when she was mauled to death by a pack of XL Bullies.

‌



Esther Martin, 68, stood little chance in what a court heard was a “tragedy waiting to happen” when she was attacked by two dogs, named Beauty and Bear, along with eight puppies of the same breed.

‌



She was at the home of her son-in-law, Ashley Warren who has now been jailed for 10 years and three months after his dog Bear was one of the dogs involved in the mauling. He was cleared of being in charge of the other dog Beauty, which belonged to his girlfriend.

‌



View 4 Images Ashley Warren is an aspiring rapper (Image: INSTAGRAM)

UK drivers getting up to £2,500 in compensation after going over potholes READ MORE :

During his trial at Chelmsford Crown Court jurors watched footage of the residential street where Ms Martin’s chilling screams could be heard among the dogs barking.

Ms Martin, who was 5ft 3in tall, had limited mobility following a hip replacement and suffered “dozens and dozens” of injuries in the attack. This included a bite through the tissue of her arm and a “complete fracturing” of the bone, the court heard

‌



“No-one would reasonably believe that Esther could control those dogs with the physicality and power that they clearly possessed, never mind the fact that there was not just one adult XL bully dog but two, with eight puppies in tow,” said prosecutor Chris Paxton KC.

He also stated: “It was, you may think, a tragedy waiting to happen, given the imbalance that arose between 68-year-old Esther, short in stature, and the towering power of these banned XL bully dogs.”

View 4 Images Ashley Warren has been jailed for more than 10 years (Image: East Anglia News Service)

‌



Warren left the animals with Ms Martin despite her mobility issues, lack of dog training and “little to no experience” of being left alone with them for a prolonged period of time.

Given that Warren had known Ms Martin for more than 12 years, he would have been aware of her mobility issues and had “no basis” to believe she could “physically stop the dogs”, said Mr Paxton.

Ms Martin’s daughter, Sonia Martin, wept as she read her victim impact statement to the court on Tuesday. “My overriding emotion is pure anger,” she said. “Anger at mum’s death, anger at Ashley Warren for forcing that situation on mum.”

‌



She said she was angry that Warren “made social media posts and songs featuring XL bullies and saying he misses them”. She added: “I can’t ever forgive Ashley Warren for his role in my mum’s death and hold him entirely responsible for the pain and suffering during her long death.

"I [will] forever hold him responsible. I hold him responsible for putting his needs above those of others and his actions will reverberate throughout our family forever.”

View 4 Images Esther Martin suffered horrific injuries during the fatal mauling (Image: PA)

‌



Another of Esther’s children, Kelly Fretwell, paid tribute to her mum, saying: “She had the best sense of humour ever and wicked laughter. She had the kindest smile.”

Giving evidence, Warren told the court he “would never have left Esther with the dogs if I thought they were dangerous” and “never thought for one second this would happen”.

Jurors also heard that the aspiring rapper had asked Ms Martin to mind the animals so he could travel to London to film a music video.

Article continues below

The mauling came two days after the Government made it a criminal offence to own an XL bully in England and Wales without a certificate of exemption.

The defendant, who wore a grey Nike hoodie and tracksuit bottoms in the dock, was also found guilty by a majority of 11 to one of having a bladed article without good reason or lawful authority at Clacton railway station on February 3 2024, after officers found a knife which he said was a prop in a music video he had been making that day in London.

News.title: Boots becomes first retailer to make major change that'll interest many people
News.content:
Boots becomes first retailer to make major change that'll interest many people

The update meets the Government’s new nutritional guidance, ahead of the 2027 target

View 3 Images Boots overhauls baby food range to help parents make healthier choices for their children (Image: Getty)

Boots has become the first national retailer to make a major change to its food range that will interest millions of people across the country. There are estimated to be 19.7 million families in the UK, with the majority residing in England, and Boots' new announcement is likely to please many mums and dads.

‌



Boots has announced a significant step forward in its mission to help parents make healthier choices for their baby’s nutrition. Now, Boots will only sell ready-made baby food products that meet the new nutritional guidelines published by the Government, making it the first major UK retailer to adopt these voluntary guidelines ahead of the target of February 2027.

‌



These guidelines are part of the Government’s wider agenda to address childhood obesity. For babies under 12 months, the new standards mandate no added sugar, sweetening ingredients or added salt in baby foods or finger foods.

‌



There are also limits on total sugar and/or fruit, and sodium content in snacks for children aged 12 months to three years. By reviewing and refining its full baby food range with the support of its nutritionists, Boots says it is making it easier for parents to feel assured that the products they choose are healthy, nutritious, and aligned with expert guidance.

Ready-to-eat baby foods play an important role for many families, offering convenience, long shelf life and ease for feeding on the go. Boots sells a large baby food selection, featuring almost 250 baby snacks, dried food and wet pouches at accessible prices from just £1.

View 3 Images Boots is the first national retailer to sell only baby food products that meet the Government’s new nutritional guidance, ahead of 2027 target (Image: PA/Boots)

‌



Vicky Pennington, Lead Nutritionist at Boots, who led the review, said: "This is an important step forward for the baby food market and for parents who want to give their children the best possible start in life. We’re trusted by millions of customers and are committed to helping parents navigate children’s nutrition.

"We know that comparing labels and understanding nutritional information can be challenging, especially when life is busy. Our aim is to make it easier for families to feel confident and know that every product they find at Boots meets high nutritional standards."

Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, Wes Streeting, said: "Families deserve to know the food they’re buying for their babies meet high nutrient standards, which is why we’ve set clear guidelines for the industry. Government can’t build a healthy society alone, it requires business, the voluntary sector, and all of us as citizens to play our part.

‌



View 3 Images The updated standards promote healthier choices by limiting sugar, sweetening ingredients and added salt for babies and young children (Image: PA/Boots)

"It is fantastic that Boots are leading the charge and no longer selling products with excessive sugar and salt. I hope other outlets will now follow the example Boots has set. Every child deserves a healthy start to life and making it easier for parents to choose healthier options is an important part of that."

Baby food brands are also reacting quickly to these new nutritional guidelines. Within its full category review, Boots has also launched several new products, including 'nutty pouches' from Ella’s Kitchen, which is also expanding its snacking range, new pots and pouches from Cow & Gate, and newly reformulated Organix Original Rice Cakes.

Article continues below

Boots will have replaced all non-compliant products in its range by mid-April. In 2022 it was one of the first retailers to ban plastic in wet wipes and later that year, it switched to only sell organic cotton wool across Boots Brand products.

News.title: Make space on your TBRs as the International Booker Prize 2026 shortlist is announced
News.content:
Make space on your TBRs as the International Booker Prize 2026 shortlist is announced

The International Booker Prize 2026 has announced the 2026 shortlist, featuring six exceptional works of translated fiction selected by a panel of experts chaired by author Natasha Brown

View 2 Images Make space on your TBRs (Image: India Hobson)

The International Booker Prize has announced 2026 shortlist, unveiling six exceptional works that represent the very best of global fiction translated into English.

‌



Chaired by award-winning author Natasha Brown, the judging panel - including Professor Marcus du Sautoy, translator Sophie Hughes, editor Troy Onyango, and novelist Nilanjana S. Roy - selected the final titles from an initial 128 submissions.

‌



The prize uniquely recognises the vital work of translation, with the £50,000 award divided equally between the winning author and translator. Each shortlisted author and translator will also receive £2,500, celebrating a selection of stories published in the UK and Ireland that transcend national borders and foster a global community of readers.

‌



The 2026 shortlist is a masterclass in narrative economy, featuring expansive stories rendered in remarkably compact forms. Only one title on the list exceeds 300 pages, while three are under 150, including the shortest entry, On Earth As It Is Beneath , which clocks in at just 101 pages.

View 2 Images The International Booker Prize 2026 shortlist is announced (Image: India Hobson)

These lean but powerful works transport readers across time and geography, from Japan-ruled Taiwan in the 1930s and Nazi-controlled Europe to the domestic magic of 1990s France and the enduring echoes of the Iranian Revolution.

‌



The characters are equally vivid, featuring a suburban witch, a morally compromised filmmaker, and a "sworn virgin" from the Albanian Alps, all of whom inhabit narratives that draw on real moments from history for their inspiration.

The six books vying for the top honour are The Nights Are Quiet in Tehran by Shida Bazyar (translated by Ruth Martin), She Who Remains by Rene Karabash (translated by Izidora Angel), The Director by Daniel Kehlmann (translated by Ross Benjamin), On Earth As It Is Beneath by Ana Paula Maia (translated by Padma Viswanathan), The Witch by Marie NDiaye (translated by Jordan Stump), and Taiwan Travelogue by Yáng Shuāng-zǐ (translated by Lin King).

Want to hear the latest books news and reviews from The Mirror's resident bookworm? Follow Aimée Walsh on Tiktok and Instagram

‌



This diverse list represents languages ranging from Bulgarian and Mandarin Chinese to Portuguese and German, showcasing a rich variety of international perspectives.

Reflecting on the selection, Natasha Brown, International Booker Prize 2026 Chair of judges, said: "Our shortlist offers readers a six-stop tour of highlights from the world of translated fiction. With narratives that capture moments from across the past century, these books reverberate with history.

‌



"While there’s heartbreak, brutality, and isolation among these stories, their lasting effect is energising. Rereading each book, we judges found hope, insight and burning humanity – along with unforgettable characters to whom I’m sure readers will return again and again.

"Make space on your TBRs; this is an unmissable reading list," she added.

The final winner will be announced on Tuesday, 19 May 2026, during a ceremony at the Tate Modern in London, which will be livestreamed on the Booker Prizes social media channels.

Article continues below

Love reading? Join Dr Aimée Walsh and our community of fellow readers in the Mirror Book Club to dive deeper into the books everyone is talking about.

News.title: 'My son's only meningitis symptom was feeling cold - hours later he was dead'
News.content:
'My son's only meningitis symptom was feeling cold - hours later he was dead'

A 'strong, healthy young man' complained to his mum about feeling cold before work but he tragically died 48 hours later after contracting meningitis B

View 3 Images Jack Bolam with his sisters (Image: Joanne Bolam / SWNS)

A heartbroken mum has shared how her teenage son died after contracting meningitis when the only symptom he showed was feeling cold.

‌



Jack Bolam, 19, said he felt chilly before heading to work one day but sadly he did 48 hours later, due to meningitis B. His mum Joanne, 49, revealed her son showed no symptoms until he arrived home early from work at a retail store, because he felt dizzy and ill.

‌



Jack was quickly taken to Royal Victoria Infirmary, in Newcastle-upon-Tyne after he started to vomit and had seizures. Doctors put the 19-year-old into an induced coma but less than 48 hours later he sadly died.

‌



View 3 Images Jack with his mum, dad and sisters (Image: Joanne Bolam / SWNS)

Chemistry nightclub at centre of deadly meningitis outbreak reopens — but with a warning READ MORE :

The mother is now warning other parents be vigilant and react quickly if they notice symptoms following the recent outbreak of the infection in Kent - which killed two young people. Jack's family were told there was no activity in his brain and his life support machine was switched off on February 1, 2025.

Support worker Joanne said: "There was no warning, no rash and no symptoms other than him feeling cold. He just had a bit of a chill - what you would usually give someone paracetamol for. Jack went to work at 5.50pm. He rang his sister at 6.40pm to say he felt dizzy and could she pick him up.

‌



"He was home 10 minutes later and I tucked him up in bed with a cup of tea as he said he was freezing. At 8pm he had vomited and his sister was saying ‘get up, mam’s coming up’. Myself and Jack’s dad and sisters went upstairs to see what was wrong. I said 'at least if you're finished early you can have your tea early'. He said 'Aye I'm pleased'. That was the last thing he said.

View 3 Images Jack Bolam with his friends (Image: Joanne Bolam / SWNS)

"Jack started convulsing so we rang 999. He was admitted to the Royal Victoria Infirmary at 9pm. At 10pm the consultant suggested I get my husband there straight away. By 11pm Jack was in the Intensive Care Unit. The consultant then told us Jack wasn't responding to treatment. Jack was on monitors - there were machines and tubes everywhere. That was Thursday January 30, 2025."

‌



The mum shared the final moments she had with her son before he tragically died. She added: "We couldn't get our heads around what was going on. Friday was a complete blur. So much information to take in. But we sat holding Jack’s hands, kissing him and talking to him like everything was okay.

"On Saturday February 1, 2025, we were asked to go and sit in whilst doctors did their final checks on our beautiful boy. Jack was pronounced dead at 2.05pm whilst his sisters and friends sat in the room across the hall.

"Family and Jack’s closest friends wanted to say goodbye and so on Sunday, February 2, we as a family decided to turn Jack's life support off. That day I will never forget.

‌



"The next three weeks were filled with visitors and Jack’s friends calling in. His best friend arrived from Australia. How we got through it I will never know."

Mum Joanna revealed her son was a "strong, healthy young man" before he contracted meningitis B who was "just at the beginning of his life". She said: "He played rugby three times a week, went to the gym four times a week. How did this happen? He had all his vaccines."

Joanne says her world was "totally destroyed" by her son's death. She added: “How we live now is completely different. People say it will get easier but it doesn't. We miss our son and brother immensely and the Jack-sized hole in our hearts will never repair.

Article continues below

"Our whole world has been totally devastated and we're broken by this awful disease. All Jack’s vaccinations were up to date and I don't understand why all bacterial meningitis isn't covered by vaccines. I just want other parents to be aware even if there's no obvious symptoms at first. You know your child and if something isn't right."

The menB jab was introduced on the NHS for babies in 2015, meaning the majority of young people born before then are not protected against it unless they have had the vaccine privately.

The family raised over £8,000 for the charity Meningitis Now over the weekend. Anyone wishing to donate can continue to do so HERE.

News.title: 'I went for a trip to my local shops and couldn't believe what I saw'
News.content:
'I went for a trip to my local shops and couldn't believe what I saw'

Being from Portsmouth, the best place to head to go shopping is Gunwharf Quays However, I made a very unexpected finding when I hit the shops at the weekend

I went to local shops and didn't expect to see what I did

Most of us expect to see a find a few bargains when hitting our local shops or even a few food stalls these days, however I got an unexpected surprise when I went shopping at the weekend.

‌



Being from Portsmouth, the best place to head to go shopping is Gunwharf Quays, seeing as the high street is pretty dead these days. The waterfront designer outlet is best known for its collection of over 90 outlet stores offering discounts of up to 60% off RRP. This includes top brands such as Polo Ralph Lauren, Hugo Boss, Nike, Adidas, Mulberry, and Kate Spade.

‌



As well as shops, there's also more than 30 restaurants and cafes, including Wagamama, Nando's, Brasserie Blanc, Giggling Squid, and Loch Fyne.

‌



View 3 Images I got a surprise on my latest trip to Gunwharf Quays (stock image) (Image: Finnbarr Webster, Getty Images)

You can also find the Spinnaker Tower there, which is a 170-metre tall landmark offering panoramic views of the Solent and Isle of Wight.

There's also a 14-screen Vue Cinema, a 26-lane Hollywood Bowl, a Grosvenor Casino, and the Aspex contemporary art gallery.

‌



You can take powerboat rides too, enjoy harbour tours, or simply walk along the marina to see visiting yachts.

As you can tell, there's a lot going on so it always attracts plenty of visitors. In fact, according to reports, Gunwharf attracts approximately 7.3 million visitors per year

As of 2025, it remains the most popular attraction in Portsmouth, visited by nearly 65% of all people who travel to the city.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Considering these stats, it's no surprise that many brands decide to promote their products there.

This includes Dr Pepper who were promoting their brand new limited-edition flavour 'Cream Swirl' last Sunday (March 29) when I visited. However, I got quite the shock when I saw how they were promoting it.

‌



As I turned the corner to head toward Boots, I was greeted by some poor guy dressed up as the fizzy drink can himself.

He was seen greeting customers as he promoted with the drink, with many people taking photos and videos as they couldn't help giggle at the poor guy.

Bizarrely they also had a man on a human hamster wheel too, with the slogan, 'Do you dare to cream?', above it. Basically the whole thing felt like a fever dream.

‌



3 View 3 Images I felt like I was in a fever dream (Image: Samantha Bartlett) 3 View 3 Images They were promoting the new Dr Pepper Cream Swirl flavour (Image: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP))

Despite the marketing being questionable, I guess it had the desired affect as I took straight to TikTok to share what I had seen with others.

Article continues below

The new 'Cream Swirl' flavour, which launched in the UK on February 23, 2026, blends the signature 23-flavour taste of Dr Pepper with a "silky creamy twist" and is scheduled to be available until February 2027

The drink has rolled out to major supermarkets and convenience stores across the country, including Tesco, Sainsbury's and Morrisons.

Maybe we should all just buy it so the flavour will be a success and that poor guy in the suit doesn't have to go out to any shopping malls anymore!

News.title: Prince Harry will not see King Charles during his father's controversial US state visit
News.content:
Prince Harry will not see King Charles during his father's controversial US state visit

A source close to the Duke of Sussex has confirmed that he will not travel to the country’s capital to see his father during his upcoming trip to the United States

View 4 Images Prince Harry with King Charles (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Prince Harry will not see King Charles when he heads to America in April for his controversial US state visit. A source close to the Duke of Sussex confirmed that he will not travel to Washington DC, where Charles will be hosted by President Trump, in order to see his father.

‌



The King’s stateside visit was confirmed today in a statement from Buckingham Palace after months of speculation over whetherthe trip would go ahead. The Palace confirmed that Charles and Camilla will visit the United States next month on advice of the government and at the invitation of the president.

‌



King Charles urged to meet Jeffrey Epstein victims on US visit by lawmaker READ MORE :

View 4 Images Prince Harry will not see King Charles during his upcoming trip to America (Image: Getty Images)

‌



It is understood the trip will take place in the last week of April, with Charles also set to visit the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda, without Camilla, after leaving the US.

While in America, the King and Queen will commemorate the 250th anniversary of American independence, attend a glittering state dinner at the White House, and the King will address Congress. Exact dates and details have yet to be disclosed.

Today Buckingham Palace said in a statement: "On advice of His Majesty’s Government, and at the invitation of The President of the United States, The King and Queen will undertake a State Visit to the United States of America.

‌



"Their Majesties’ programme will celebrate the historic connections and the modern bilateral relationship between the United Kingdom and the United States, marking the 250th anniversary of American Independence. The King will then continue to Bermuda to undertake His Majesty’s first Royal Visit as Monarch to a British Overseas Territory."

View 4 Images Harry last saw his father in London in September 2025 (Image: PA)

It is believed Charles and Camilla will only spend a few days stateside, sticking to the East Coast of the country with events taking place in Washington DC and New York. Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, along with their children Archie and Lilibet, reside in California, on the West Coast. Harry last saw his father in September last year during a whirlwind trip to the UK for the WellChild Awards.

‌



Former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond previously told the Mirror that Charles’ jam-packed schedule would prevent the father and son from having a meeting while the King is stateside.

She said: "State visits are incredibly busy. The schedule is worked out months in advance and is tightly packed with carefully curated engagements designed to enhance bilateral relations. There is very little downtime, and I can’t think that the King would fly across the whole country to visit Harry and his family in California."

Jennie said that Charles would no doubt welcome a meeting with his son and his grandchildren - whom he has only met a few times - but time would not allow it.

‌



View 4 Images Charles will be hosted by President Trump in the US in April (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

She said: "I’m sure Charles would love to meet his grandchildren again… But visits like this are about as official as it can get, and it’s really not a time for patching up severely strained family relationships. A meeting would also inevitably draw the headlines away from the purpose of the visit. It’s far more likely that Harry and his family will be encouraged to keep a low profile during the trip.”

Article continues below

It will be the King’s first visit to the US as monarch and the first state visit by a British sovereign to America for nearly 20 years, since Queen Elizabeth II’s tour in 2007. In the hours after the visit was confirmed, US president Donald Trump said: "This momentous occasion will be even more special this year, as we commemorate the 250th Anniversary of our Great Country. I look forward to spending time with the King, whom I greatly respect. It will be TERRIFIC!"

News.title: 'I was forced to remove my eyeball after nightmare Mexico holiday pool accident'
News.content:
'I was forced to remove my eyeball after nightmare Mexico holiday pool accident'

WARNING: GRAPHIC CONTENT A dad said his eye had to be removed after an accident while playing in the pool on holiday left him with blood streaming down his face

View 5 Images Lee lost his eye after a family holiday (Image: Jam Press)

A British dad has been "forced" to remove his eyeball after it was slashed with a stranger's fingernail during a nightmare holiday accident.

‌



Lee Cuthbert had been playing volleyball with his kids, Mia, now 15, and Charlie, now 18, in their hotel's pool while away on a two week all inclusive holiday in Mexico. Other holidaymakers joined in their match, but disaster struck when the 46-year-old was left with blood streaming from his right eye.

‌



His wife, Rachael, 41, was "horrified" at the sight, especially when she opened husband's eyelid to see the damage. Rachael, a patient services advisor, from Leicester, said: "I gasped with horror as I saw his eye.

‌



View 5 Images Lee and Rachael in Mexico after the accident (Image: Jam Press)

" He told me one of the other players had caught him with their nail when they reached out for the ball. It dug in and slashed his eye right in the middle. I couldn't help but panic as I rushed to find help."

After the accident, in October 2017, a nurse was thankfully nearby and urged the family to rush to hospital. Rachael stayed with the kids, as Lee's parents rushed him to medics. The wife, added that she only realised the true gravity of his accident when Lee returned to his family the next morning.

‌



View 5 Images The dad was 'forced' to have his eyeball removed (Image: Jam Press)

She said: "He had a huge bandage covering his eye. It was stitched back together, but it was only temporary. When the player hit him, his eyeball exploded instantly.

"Lee would never get his sight back and it took a while for him to accept this. It was red raw inside as I cleaned it carefully. Our trip had been ruined as he had to stay cooped up in the bedroom away from any sunlight or water."

‌



View 5 Images His eye was slashed by a stranger's fingernail while playing volleyball (Image: Jam Press)

The family were told to fly back to the UK just a week into their Mexico trip. Daily tasks, such as making a cup of tea, became impossible as Lee wasn't able to see what he was doing properly.

A year later, the dad had to get the iris part of his eye removed and replaced with a prosthetic. The bricklayer however said his anxiety started to subside because the result looked "so real".

Article continues below

View 5 Images Lee was rushed to hospital while in Mexico (Image: Jam Press)

The family filed a claim through their insurer, who paid out £15,000 and they said they have come to terms with their new normal, adding that Lee is not afraid to play in pools. Rachael added: "He still loves snorkelling or playing water games. He's quickly returned to my daredevil hubby."

News.title: Glasgow tower block tragedy as man plunges to death and cops lock down area
News.content:
Glasgow tower block tragedy as man plunges to death and cops lock down area

A man has died after falling from a tower block, with police having launched a probe into the horrifying incident.

Emergency services were called to the high-rise at Dougrie Place in Glasgow's Castlemilk area at around 5.25am this morning. The man was sadly pronounced dead at the scene, with officers carrying out enquiries to establish the circumstances surrounding his passing. The man's relatives have been informed.

Police say they are treating the death as unexplained, with an investigation into the incident now underway.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "Around 5.25am on Tuesday, 31 March, 2026, police received a report a man had fallen from a flat in Dougrie Place, Glasgow. Emergency services attended and the man was pronounced dead at the scene. His next of kin has been informed.

"The death is being treated as unexplained and enquiries are ongoing."
